mainTopic: Missed ברכות, the drink אספרגוס, angelic warnings, and the ten laws of the כוס של ברכה
overview: The amud opens by explaining why food must be spat out before a ברכה: 'יִמָּלֵא פִי תְּהִלָּתֶךָ' teaches that the whole mouth should be free for praise. Next, רב חסדא rules with a garlic משל that someone who began eating without a ברכה should bless now rather than keep eating. רבינא tries to extend this to after the meal, using the ברכה on טבילה as proof, but the גמרא rejects him: since the eater could have blessed beforehand, once he missed it, הואיל ואידחי אידחי. The גמרא then turns to אספרגוס, a morning drink usually made of wine. It discusses the drink's health effects, six rules for drinking it, and several contradictions, which are solved by aged versus new wine and by wine-based versus beer-based kinds. Three warnings from סוריאל and from the מלאך המות follow, along with remedies for someone who meets women returning from a funeral. Finally, the גמרא lists ten things said about the כוס של ברכה, notes that רבי יוחנן keeps only four, praises a full cup, and explains עיטור, עיטוף, and holding the cup with both hands. The amud ends with an unresolved question about whether the left hand may help the right, and רב אשי's practical ruling on it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not just move non-disgusting food aside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions why one must spit out food that would not become disgusting. Why not just push it to the side of the mouth and say the ברכה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Even with food that does not become disgusting, let him just push it to one side of his mouth and say the ברכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier rule that someone with food in his mouth must spit it out before making a ברכה. For food that wouldn't become gross if taken out and put back, why not just tuck it into his cheek and bless?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion allowed different handling depending on whether food becomes מאוס (disgusting) once removed. The גמרא now asks: if disgust is not an issue, why remove it at all? Shifting it aside seems good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: an item, a thing (here: a piece of food)

phrases.english: With an item that does not become disgusting as well,
phrases.notes: This points back to the case of food in the mouth from the previous amud.

phrases.english: let him shift it to one side and recite the blessing?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִידֵּי דְּלָא מִמְּאִיס נָמֵי, לְסַלְּקִינְהוּ לְצַד אֶחָד וְלִיבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous part of the daf about food in the mouth during a ברכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement to spit out food before saying a ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only concern is the food becoming disgusting, then for food that doesn't become disgusting, moving it aside should be enough.

steps.title: A blessing needs a full mouth
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק קסקסאה, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains that the reason is the פסוק 'יִמָּלֵא פִי תְּהִלָּתֶךָ': the mouth must be fully available for praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק קסקסאה explained it before רבי יוסי בר אבין in the name of רבי יוחנן: because the פסוק says, 'My mouth will be filled with Your praise.'
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given. Moving the food aside is not enough, because the פסוק teaches that one's whole mouth should be filled with praise of ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes the reason behind the rule. It is not only about disgust. It is about the dignity of the ברכה. If food is tucked in the cheek, the mouth is only half-free, so it must come out completely.

keyTerms.meaning: 'My mouth will be filled with Your praise' (תהלים ע״א:ח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic principle: a ברכה should be said with a clear, unobstructed mouth, out of respect for ה׳.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak Kaskesa'a explained it
before Rabbi Yosei bar Avin
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
because it is stated:
"My mouth will be filled with Your praise."
phrases.notes: Your whole mouth, not half of it, should be used for praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב יִצְחָק קַסְקְסָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason to spit out food is that it might become disgusting, so moving it aside should suffice.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mouth must be completely free for the ברכה, based on 'יִמָּלֵא פִי תְּהִלָּתֶךָ'.

steps.title: Ate without a blessing: can he still bless?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא is asked: if someone ate and drank without saying the ברכה first, can he go back and say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב חסדא: someone who ate and drank and did not say a ברכה, can he go back and say it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. Someone forgot the ברכה ראשונה and already started eating. Can he still say it now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה is supposed to come before eating. So the question is whether a 'late' ברכה has any value, or whether the chance is lost once he has started.

keyTerms.meaning: that he go back and bless

phrases.english: They asked Rav Chisda:
One who ate and drank and did not recite a blessing,
what is the law, may he go back and recite the blessing?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, still about ברכות on food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person who started eating without a ברכה can still say it afterward.

steps.title: The garlic משל: don't make it worse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers with a משל: if you ate garlic and your breath smells, would you eat more garlic to keep it smelling? So too, don't keep eating without a ברכה. Bless now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: someone who ate garlic and his breath smells, should he go eat another garlic so his breath will keep smelling?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers with a rhetorical question. Having already done wrong by not blessing, you shouldn't keep eating without a ברכה. You should say it now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garlic stands for eating without a ברכה, and the smell stands for the wrongdoing. Continuing to eat without blessing would be like eating more garlic, adding to the problem. So the answer is yes: go back and bless for what you still eat.

keyTerms.meaning: his smell spreads; his breath smells

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the garlic line as a real question about garlic. It is a משל, a rhetorical 'of course not!' that means: don't keep eating without a ברכה, go back and bless.

phrases.english: He said to them: One who ate garlic
and his odor smells,
should he go back and eat another garlic
so that his odor will smell?!
phrases.notes: Of course not! So he should fix it by saying the ברכה right now.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי שֶׁאָכַל שׁוּם וְרֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question posed to רב חסדא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. One who has not finished eating should go back and say the ברכה rather than keep eating without one.

steps.title: רבינא: even after the meal, bless
steps.stepSummary: רבינא draws a conclusion from רב חסדא's answer: even if the person already finished his meal, he should still go back and say the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: therefore, even if he finished his meal, he goes back and says the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא extends רב חסדא's ruling further. It applies not only in the middle of eating but even after the whole meal is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's answer is about someone still eating. רבינא understands the principle as 'a missed ברכה can still be made up,' so he applies it even when nothing more will be eaten. This extension is what the גמרא will soon test.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Therefore,
even if he finished his meal, he goes back and recites the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: הִלְכָּךְ אֲפִילּוּ גָּמַר סְעוּדָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב חסדא's answer and pushes it further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after finishing the meal, one who forgot the ברכה ראשונה should go back and say it.

steps.title: Proof from the blessing on immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a ברייתא: someone who immerses in a מקוה says the ברכה on טבילה as he comes up, after the act is already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: one who immersed and came up says, as he comes up, 'Blessed... Who sanctified us with His מצוות and commanded us about immersion.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא supports his ruling with a source. Here is a case where a ברכה is said after the action, so a ברכה after eating should also work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a ברכה comes before the act (עובר לעשייתן). The ברייתא shows that by טבילה, the ברכה is said afterward. רבינא uses this to argue that a ברכה after the fact is acceptable for food too.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who immersed and came up,
says as he comes up:
"Blessed... Who has sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us about immersion."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: טָבַל וְעָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a source for רבינא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's ruling that a ברכה can be said even after finishing the meal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the ברכה on טבילה is said after coming up from the water.

steps.title: Rejection: immersion is a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבינא's proof. At a טבילה the person couldn't bless beforehand because he was impure. Someone eating could have blessed beforehand, and once he missed it, the chance is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, from the start the man was not fit to bless. Here, from the start the man was fit. Since he was pushed off, he stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the comparison to טבילה. With it, רבינא's extension falls: after finishing the meal, one does not go back and say the ברכה ראשונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By טבילה the ברכה is delayed only because a טמא person could not bless before immersing. The delay was built in. Someone eating was able to bless beforehand and didn't, so once the meal is over he is דחוי. The rule 'הואיל ואידחי, אידחי' means that once the opportunity is lost, it is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: but that is not so (rejection formula)
once it was pushed off, it stays pushed off

steps.whatToRemember: If someone forgot the ברכה ראשונה and is still eating, he should bless now (רב חסדא's garlic משל). Once the meal is finished, the chance is gone. The טבילה case is different, because there the person could not bless beforehand.
steps.confusionAlert: 'ולא היא' does not reject רב חסדא. It rejects only רבינא's extension to after the meal, and his proof from טבילה. רב חסדא's ruling for someone still eating stays in place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the principle of דחייה: a ברכה that could have been said at the right time but wasn't cannot always be made up later.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
there, from the start the man was not fit,
phrases.notes: Before immersing he was impure and could not say the ברכה.

phrases.english: here, from the start the man was fit,
phrases.notes: Before eating he could have blessed.

phrases.english: and since he was pushed off, he is pushed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, הָתָם — מֵעִיקָּרָא גַּבְרָא לָא חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 6, and with it the ruling in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבינא's extension (blessing after finishing the meal) and his proof from טבילה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: At טבילה the person was unfit to bless beforehand, but someone eating was fit and missed his chance, so הואיל ואידחי, אידחי.

steps.title: The health benefits and dangers of אספרגוס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that אספרגוס is good for the heart, eyes and intestines, and good for the whole body if drunk regularly. If someone gets drunk from it, it harms the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: אספרגוס is good for the heart and good for the eyes, and even more so for the intestines. Someone who drinks it regularly finds it good for his whole body. But someone who gets drunk from it finds it harmful for his whole body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about a drink called אספרגוס and its effects on health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not the same as the vegetable asparagus. It is a drink, usually made with wine, taken in the morning before eating. The ברייתא gives a balance: drinking it in moderation is healthy, and drinking it to the point of drunkenness is harmful.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This phrase introduces a ברייתא.
A drink, usually wine-based, taken in the morning before eating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this אספרגוס with the green vegetable. Here it is a drink.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: Asparagus is good for the heart
and beneficial for the eyes,
and all the more so for the intestines.
phrases.notes: The next question is aimed at this line.

phrases.english: And for one who drinks it regularly, it is good for his whole body.
But for one who gets drunk from it, it is harmful for his whole body.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִסְפָּרָגוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It is unrelated to the discussion of the missed ברכה in steps 3 through 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אספרגוס in moderation benefits the heart, eyes, intestines and whole body. Getting drunk from it harms the whole body.

steps.title: Wine is supposed to be bad for the intestines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the ברייתא is talking about wine-based אספרגוס, since it is good for the heart. But another ברייתא says wine is good for the heart, eyes and spleen and bad for the head, intestines and hemorrhoids. So how can it be good for the intestines?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא said it is good for the heart, we can conclude that it is talking about wine. Yet it also says 'all the more so for the intestines.' But another ברייתא taught: for ל-ע-ט (heart, eyes, spleen) wine is good, and for ר-מ-ת (head, intestines, hemorrhoids) it is harmful!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between our ברייתא, which says it is good for the intestines, and a different ברייתא, which says wine is bad for the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the גמרא establishes that the drink is made of wine, because 'good for the heart' is a known quality of wine. Once we know it is wine, the other ברייתא applies, and that ברייתא puts the intestines (the מ of רמ"ת) on the harmful list. Both sources cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?' This introduces a contradicting source.
Short for לב, עינים, טחול (heart, eyes, spleen). Wine is good for these.
Short for ראש, מעים, תחתוניות (head, intestines, hemorrhoids). Wine is harmful for these.

phrases.english: From the fact that it teaches 'good for the heart,'
we can infer that we are dealing with wine,
phrases.notes: Wine is known to be good for the heart

phrases.english: and it teaches: 'and all the more so for the intestines.'
But wasn't it taught: for L-E-T (heart, eyes, spleen) it is good,
for R-M-T (head, intestines, hemorrhoids) it is harmful!
phrases.notes: The intestines are on the harmful list

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: לְלַעַ״ט — יָפֶה, לְרָמַ״ת — קָשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 8 that אספרגוס is good for the intestines.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן לִבְנֵי מֵעַיִם' in the ברייתא of step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The drink is wine-based. Another ברייתא says wine harms the intestines, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: The benefit applies to aged wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא praising the drink for the intestines is talking about aged wine (מיושן).
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was talking about aged wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different kinds of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Aged wine is good for the intestines and new wine is harmful to them. So our ברייתא is about אספרגוס made with aged wine, and the רמ"ת ברייתא is about regular new wine. Both sources are correct, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When that ברייתא was taught,' meaning it was said about a specific case

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was about aged wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הַהִיא, בִּמְיוּשָּׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: aged wine versus new wine
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All wine harms the intestines, so the ברייתא in step 8 contradicts the רמ"ת ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Aged wine helps the intestines (step 8). New wine harms them (the רמ"ת ברייתא).

steps.title: Proof from a vow against wine
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in נדרים proves that aged wine is good for the intestines. A man vowed off wine because it harms his intestines. People told him aged wine is good for them, and he stayed silent. So new wine is forbidden to him and aged wine is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: someone said, 'Wine is קונם (forbidden) for me to taste, because wine is harmful to the intestines.' People said to him, 'But isn't aged wine good for the intestines?' He was silent. So he is forbidden to drink new wine and permitted to drink aged wine. Learn from this that aged wine is good for the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support its answer that aged wine is good for the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's own reason was that wine hurts the intestines. By staying silent when told that aged wine is actually good for them, he showed that his vow never included aged wine. The halacha follows this reasoning, which proves that aged wine is accepted as good for the intestines.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word meaning 'forbidden to me like a קרבן'
'And he was silent,' meaning he accepted their point
'Learn from this.' It marks a proof as established.

steps.whatToRemember: אספרגוס made with aged wine is good for the intestines. New wine is harmful to them, as the רמ"ת ברייתא says.

phrases.english: As we learned: 'Wine is konam (forbidden) for me to taste,'
'because wine is harmful to the intestines.'
They said to him: 'But isn't aged wine'
'good for the intestines?'
If he was silent, he is forbidden to drink new wine,
and permitted to drink aged wine.
Learn from this.
phrases.notes: Aged wine is good for the intestines

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן: קֻוֽנָּם יַיִן שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 10 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that aged wine is good for the intestines
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדרים about a קונם vow on wine

steps.title: Six rules for drinking אספרגוס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists six rules for drinking אספרגוס. Drink it undiluted and from a full cup. Take it with the right hand and drink with the left. Do not talk after it and do not pause while drinking it. Return the cup only to the one who gave it. Spit afterward. Follow it only with something of its own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Six things were said about אספרגוס. You drink it only undiluted and from a full cup. You receive it in the right hand and drink it with the left. You do not talk after drinking it, and you do not stop in the middle of drinking it. You return the cup only to the person who gave it to you. You spit after it. And you follow it only with something of its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא listing practical rules for how to drink אספרגוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are health and custom guidelines, not prohibitions about איסור and היתר. They describe exactly how to drink it, from how it is served, to how it is drunk, to what you do afterward. 'Its own kind' means following it with something related, such as dates after date-based drink.
steps.confusionAlert: If you count the items, you may get more than six. Some items, such as 'right hand' and 'left hand,' or 'full' and 'undiluted,' are counted together, and the commentators discuss how the list adds up.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives detailed guidelines for drinking אספרגוס: how it is served, how it is drunk, and what to do afterward.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Six things were said about asparagus:
One does not drink it
except when it is undiluted and full;
he receives it in the right hand
and drinks it with the left;
and one does not talk after it,
and one does not pause while drinking it;
and one does not return it
except to the one who gave it to him;
and he spits after it;
and one follows it only with its own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּאִסְפָּרָגוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of אספרגוס with a new ברייתא of practical guidelines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אספרגוס is drunk undiluted and from a full cup. It is taken with the right hand and drunk with the left, without talking afterward or pausing. The cup is returned only to the giver, one spits afterward, and it is followed only by its own kind.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says to follow it only with bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from step 12, 'follow it only with something of its own kind.' Another ברייתא says to follow it only with bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: you may only follow it with bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא contradicts the last rule of step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said that after drinking אספרגוס you should follow it only with something of its own kind, such as dates after a date-based drink. This ברייתא says to follow it only with bread. Both cannot be true as stated, so the גמרא needs to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? It introduces a contradicting source.
Follow it up or support it with something eaten afterward

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: one does not follow it up
except with bread!
phrases.notes: This contradicts 'only with its own kind' from step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא אֵין סוֹמְכִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בְּפַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the final rule of the six rules in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'follow it only with its own kind' in step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite instructions about what should follow the drink.

steps.title: Wine-based versus beer-based אספרגוס
steps.stepSummary: No difficulty. One ברייתא speaks about אספרגוס made of wine and the other about אספרגוס made of beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the wine kind, and that one is about the beer kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the two ברייתות are talking about two different kinds of אספרגוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אספרגוס could be made with wine or with beer. The wine kind is followed by bread, and the beer kind is followed by more of its own kind. Since they are different drinks, the two rules do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the standard opening of an answer.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which source matches which drink. In this case, the bread rule is for the wine-based kind, and the 'own kind' rule is for the beer-based kind.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the kind made of wine,
phrases.notes: Follow it with bread.

phrases.english: that one is about the kind made of beer.
phrases.notes: Follow it with its own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בִּדְחַמְרָא, הָא בִּדְשִׁכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different type of drink
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to describe the same drink and gave opposite instructions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine kind is followed by bread, and the beer kind is followed by its own kind.

steps.title: Contradiction about which body parts it helps
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says אספרגוס is good for לב, עינים and טחול and bad for ראש, מעים and תחתוניות. Another ברייתא says the exact opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: it is good for heart, eyes and spleen and harmful for head, intestines and hemorrhoids. Another ברייתא teaches: it is good for head, intestines and hemorrhoids and harmful for heart, eyes and spleen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that flatly contradict each other about which body parts אספרגוס helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לע"ט is a memory code for לב, עינים and טחול. רמ"ת is a code for ראש, מעים and תחתוניות. Each ברייתא swaps which group is helped and which is harmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Code for לֵב, עֵינַיִם, טְחוֹל (heart, eyes, spleen)
Code for רֹאשׁ, מֵעַיִם, תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת (head, intestines, hemorrhoids)

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches: for heart, eyes and spleen it is good,
for head, intestines and hemorrhoids it is harmful.
And another ברייתא teaches:
for head, intestines and hemorrhoids it is good, for heart, eyes and spleen it is harmful!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא לְלַעַ״ט יָפֶה, לְרָמַ״ת קָשֶׁה. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new contradiction on the same subject, which will be solved with the same tool as step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about the health effects of אספרגוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each source says the opposite of the other about which organs benefit and which are harmed.

steps.title: Again, wine-based versus beer-based
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: the ברייתא that says it is good for לע"ט means the wine kind, and the other means the beer kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the wine kind, and that one is about the beer kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the second contradiction with the same distinction between wine and beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine kind helps the heart, eyes and spleen, which fits step 9, where wine itself was said to be good for them. The beer kind has the reverse effect.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the kind made of wine,
phrases.notes: Good for לע"ט.

phrases.english: that one is about the kind made of beer.
phrases.notes: Good for רמ"ת.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בִּדְחַמְרָא, הָא בִּדְשִׁכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of drink
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to describe one drink with opposite effects.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine kind is good for לע"ט, and the beer kind is good for רמ"ת.

steps.title: Contradiction about spitting afterward
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says that if he spits after drinking it, he gets sick. Another says that if he does not spit, he gets sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: if he spat after it, he suffers. Another ברייתא teaches: if he did not spit after it, he suffers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third contradiction, this time about whether one should spit after drinking אספרגוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 listed 'spit afterward' as one of the rules. Here one ברייתא says spitting causes harm, and another says not spitting causes harm. These are direct opposites.

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches:
If he spat after it, he suffers.
And another ברייתא teaches:
If he did not spit after it, he suffers!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: רָק אַחֲרָיו לוֹקֶה. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel contradiction, related to the spitting rule of step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about spitting after drinking אספרגוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source says spitting harms, and the other says not spitting harms.

steps.title: Once more, wine-based versus beer-based
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: spitting harms with the wine kind, and not spitting harms with the beer kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the wine kind, and that one is about the beer kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the third contradiction with the same wine and beer distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the wine kind, spitting afterward causes harm. With the beer kind, failing to spit causes harm. All three contradictions disappear once we know which drink is being discussed.
steps.whatToRemember: Three contradictions about אספרגוס (what follows it, which organs it helps, and spitting) are all solved the same way: one source means the wine kind (דחמרא) and the other means the beer kind (דשכרא).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the kind made of wine,
phrases.notes: Spitting harms.

phrases.english: that one is about the kind made of beer.
phrases.notes: Not spitting harms.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בִּדְחַמְרָא, הָא בִּדְשִׁכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of drink
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to describe one drink with opposite instructions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spitting harms with the wine kind, and not spitting harms with the beer kind.

steps.title: One may spit even before the king
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that since not spitting can cause illness, a person may spit even in front of a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Now that you said that if he did not spit after it he suffers, its water (the saliva) may be spat out even in front of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the rule just learned and draws a practical conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it is disrespectful to spit in front of a king. Since not spitting after this drink is a health danger, health comes first, and he may spit even there.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you said. It builds a new rule on an earlier statement.
Its water, meaning the saliva after drinking

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a health danger overrides normal rules of respect and good manners.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Now that you have said
that if he did not spit after it he suffers,
its water (the saliva) may be spat out
even in front of the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ לֹא רָק אַחֲרָיו לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the ברייתא that not spitting causes illness
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because not spitting after (beer-based) אספרגוס is harmful, one may spit even before a king.

steps.title: סוריאל's three warnings to רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע reports that the angel סוריאל told him three things to avoid: taking a shirt from a servant in the morning and putting it on, washing hands from someone who has not washed his own hands, and returning a cup of אספרגוס to anyone except the person who gave it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע said: סוריאל, the minister of the Divine Presence, told me three things. Do not take your shirt in the morning from your servant's hand and put it on. Do not have your hands washed by someone who has not washed his own hands. Do not hand back a cup of אספרגוס to anyone except the one who gave it to you.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was just discussing the drink אספרגוס, it now brings a related teaching. In it, an angel lists three things a person should avoid, and one of them involves a cup of אספרגוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement linked to the previous discussion by its subject. It gives three practical warnings. The reason for all three comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Minister of the Divine Presence, a title for a high-ranking angel

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha said:
Three things were told to me by
Suriel, the minister of the Divine Presence:
Do not take your shirt in the morning
from the hand of the servant and put it on.
And do not wash your hands
from one who has not washed his own hands.
And do not return a cup of asparagus drink
except to the one who gave it to you

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים סָח לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by subject: the previous steps discussed אספרגוס, and this statement includes a warning about a cup of אספרגוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three things to avoid: putting on a shirt handed over by a servant in the morning, having one's hands washed by someone who has not washed his own hands, and returning a cup of אספרגוס to someone other than the person who gave it.

steps.title: The reason: harmful forces wait for these moments
steps.stepSummary: סוריאל explains that a band of harmful forces (some say destructive angels) waits for a person to fall into one of these three situations so that they can catch him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that a band of harmful forces, and some say a troop of destructive angels, waits for a person and says: When will this person get into one of these situations, so that he can be caught?
steps.whatsHappening: The angel now gives the reason behind the three warnings from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three warnings share one reason. Each situation is a moment of exposure that harmful forces are waiting for. The words וְאָמְרִי לַהּ show two versions of what exactly these forces are, but the message is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: A band or group (of harmful forces)

phrases.english: Because a band (of harmful forces),
and some say, a troop
of destructive angels,
lie in wait for a person
and say: When will a person come
into one of these situations
and be caught?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁתַּכְסְפִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the three warnings in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Harmful forces wait for a person to fall into one of these three situations so that they can catch him.

steps.title: The מלאך המות's three warnings to רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reports three warnings from the מלאך המות. The first two match סוריאל's warnings. The third is new: do not stand in front of women returning from a funeral, because the מלאך המות dances before them with his sword and has permission to harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The מלאך המות told me three things. Do not take your shirt in the morning from your servant and put it on. Do not have your hands washed by someone who has not washed his own hands. Do not stand in front of women when they are coming back from a funeral, because I dance in front of them with my sword in my hand, and I have permission to destroy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel teaching of three warnings, this time from the מלאך המות. The third warning is different from סוריאל's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the warnings repeat exactly, which strengthens them. The third warning replaces the אספרגוס cup with standing before women returning from a funeral. In that situation the מלאך המות is actively present and allowed to harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Returning from the dead person, meaning from a funeral or burial

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mistake this for the same list as סוריאל's. Only the first two items match; the third item is completely different.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים סָח לִי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת:
phrases.english: The Angel of Death told me three things:
Do not take your shirt in the morning
from the hand of the servant and put it on.
And do not wash your hands
from one who has not washed his own hands.
And do not stand in front of the women
at the time when they return from the dead (a funeral),
because I come dancing in front of them
with my sword in my hand
and I have permission to destroy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים סָח לִי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list of three warnings. It repeats two items from step 20 and adds a new third item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid the shirt-from-servant and the washing-from-the-unwashed situations, and do not stand before women returning from a funeral.

steps.title: What if he meets them anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if someone does meet women coming back from a funeral, what should he do to protect himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he does meet them, what is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the third warning. This sets up the list of remedies that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning told us what to avoid, but sometimes a person cannot avoid it. The גמרא wants to know what someone can do once he is already in that situation.

phrases.english: And if he encountered them, what is his remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי פָּגַע, מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical follow-up to the third warning in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a person should do if he cannot avoid meeting women returning from a funeral.

steps.title: The remedies: move away, cross, hide, or recite a verse
steps.stepSummary: He should jump four אמות from his place. If there is a river, he should cross it. If there is another road, he should take it. If there is a wall, he should stand behind it. If none of these is available, he should turn his face away and recite the פסוק "ויאמר ה׳ אל השטן יגער ה׳ בך" until the women pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should jump four אמות away from where he is standing. If there is a river, he should cross it. If there is another road, he should go on it. If there is a wall, he should stand behind it. If none of these is available, he should turn his face away and say: "And ה׳ said to the שטן‎: ה׳ will rebuke you..." until they have passed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a list of options, from the most physical (getting away) to the last resort (turning away and reciting a פסוק).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each remedy puts distance or a barrier between the person and the danger: four אמות, a river, another road, or a wall. If no physical escape exists, he turns his face away and uses a פסוק in which ה׳ rebukes the שטן, as spiritual protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, a person's immediate personal space
ה׳ will rebuke you (a פסוק in זכריה)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of remedies: move four אמות, cross a river, take another road, stand behind a wall, and as a last resort turn away and say "יגער ה׳ בך" until they pass.

phrases.english: He should jump four cubits from his place;
if there is a river, let him cross it;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִיכָּא דַּרְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא — לֵיזִיל בַּהּ,
phrases.english: and if there is another road, let him go on it;
and if there is a wall, let him stand behind it;
and if not, let him turn his face away and say:
"And the Lord said to the Satan:
The Lord rebukes you, etc."
until they pass by him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִינְשׁוֹף מִדּוּכְתֵּיהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ranked list of protections: jump four אמות, cross a river, take another road, stand behind a wall, or turn away and recite "יגער ה׳ בך" until the women pass.

steps.title: Ten things said about the cup of blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רבי אבהו (or, some say, a ברייתא) lists ten requirements for the כוס של ברכה: rinsing and washing, undiluted and full, עיטור and עיטוף, taking it with two hands and placing it in the right hand, lifting it a טפח from the ground, and looking at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אבהו, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: Ten things were said about the כוס של ברכה. It needs rinsing and washing. It must be undiluted and full. It needs adorning and wrapping. He takes it with both hands and then holds it in his right hand. He lifts it a טפח off the ground, and he keeps his eyes on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a brand-new topic, the special cup of wine used for ברכת המזון, and lists ten things required for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is a way of showing honor to the cup over which the ברכה is said: it is clean, full, and handled carefully with attention. The items are listed briefly here, and the גמרא will explain what several of them mean later on.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of wine over which a ברכה (such as ברכת המזון) is said
Rinsing the inside and washing the outside (as the ברייתא in step 28 defines them)
Undiluted wine, and filled to the top
Adorning (surrounding) and wrapping (covering oneself), explained later in the גמרא
It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The pairs (rinsing/washing, undiluted/full, adorning/wrapping) each count as two separate items. That is how the list adds up to ten.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Abbahu said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּכוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה:
phrases.english: Ten things were said about a cup of blessing:
It requires rinsing and washing.
Undiluted and full.
Adorning and wrapping.
He takes it with his two hands,
and places it in the right hand.
And he lifts it a handbreadth from the ground,
and fixes his eyes on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּכוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, not dependent on the previous discussion of harmful forces.
steps.whyThisMatters: These ten details form the basis for how the כוס של ברכה is handled in practice, and the גמרא goes on to explain them one by one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כוס של ברכה requires: הדחה, שטיפה, חי, מלא, עיטור, עיטוף, taking it with both hands, placing it in the right hand, lifting it a טפח, and looking at it.

steps.title: Some add: sending the cup to his household
steps.stepSummary: יש אומרים add one more practice: after the ברכה, he also sends the cup as a gift to the members of his household.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he also sends it as a gift to the members of his household.
steps.whatsHappening: An additional opinion adds one more practice to the list of how to treat the כוס של ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten items in the main list cover preparing and holding the cup. The יש אומרים view adds what happens afterward: the cup's blessing is shared with his family by sending it to them as a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces an additional or alternative opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: The כוס של ברכה has ten listed requirements, and according to יש אומרים it is also sent to one's household as a gift.

phrases.english: And some say: he also sends it
as a gift to the members of his household.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מְשַׁגְּרוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה לְאַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more practice to the list in step 25, according to another opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to יש אומרים, one also sends the כוס של ברכה as a gift to his household.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן keeps only four of the ten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that in practice only four of the ten cup requirements apply to 'us': הדחה, שטיפה, חי, and מלא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We only have four of them: rinsing, washing, undiluted, and full.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows down the list of ten requirements from step 25. He says that 'we' practice only four of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 gave a list of ten things done with the כוס של ברכה. רבי יוחנן says that in his practice only four are kept: the two cleaning steps (הדחה, שטיפה), wine that is חי, and a cup that is מלא. The other six are not part of his required practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Undiluted wine, straight from the barrel

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the other six practices are wrong. He is saying that in practice 'we' keep only these four.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעָה בִּלְבַד:
phrases.english: We have only four alone:
phrases.notes: Out of the ten listed in step 25.

phrases.english: Rinsing, washing, undiluted, and full.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעָה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the list of ten requirements from step 25 to four that apply in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, only four of the ten apply: הדחה, שטיפה, חי, מלא.

steps.title: Rinsing is inside, washing is outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the difference between the two cleaning steps: הדחה cleans the inside of the cup and שטיפה cleans the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: rinsing is on the inside, and washing is on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains two words from the list so we know they are two different actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this explanation, הדחה and שטיפה might look like two names for the same thing. The ברייתא shows that each refers to a different part of the cup: הדחה is the inside and שטיפה is the outside.

phrases.english: It was taught: rinsing is from the inside,
and washing is from the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הֲדָחָה מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the first two of רבי יוחנן's four requirements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הדחה cleans the inside of the cup; שטיפה cleans the outside.

steps.title: A full cup earns a boundless inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that whoever makes a ברכה over a full cup is given a 'boundless inheritance,' learned from a פסוק about נפתלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whoever makes a blessing over a full cup is given an inheritance with no borders, as it says: 'Full of the blessing of ה׳, inherit the sea and the south.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן describes the reward for using a full cup, one of his four requirements, and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the word 'full' (ומלא) with 'the blessing of ה׳' and with inheriting in many directions (ים ודרום). From this רבי יוחנן learns that a full cup of ברכה brings an inheritance without limits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who blesses over a full cup —
they give him an inheritance without borders,
as it says: 'And full of the blessing of ה׳,'
'inherit the sea and the south.'
phrases.notes: דברים לג:כג, from the ברכה to נפתלי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמְבָרֵךְ עַל כּוֹס מָלֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on מלא, one of the four requirements, by describing its reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessing over a full cup earns a boundless inheritance.

steps.title: He inherits two worlds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says that one who blesses over a full cup inherits both עולם הזה and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says: He merits and inherits two worlds, this world and the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא describes the reward for a full cup differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן described the reward as land without borders. רבי יוסי בר חנינא describes it as two whole worlds. Both agree that a full cup brings a great reward.
steps.whatToRemember: A full כוס של ברכה is highly praised: it brings a boundless inheritance (רבי יוחנן) or both worlds (רבי יוסי בר חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina says:
He merits and inherits two worlds,
this world and the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹכֶה וְנוֹחֵל שְׁנֵי עוֹלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different description of the full-cup reward from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessing over a full cup earns both עולם הזה and עולם הבא.

steps.title: How the cup was adorned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains עיטור using two practices: רב יהודה surrounded the cup with students, and רב חסדא surrounded it with other cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: Adorning: רב יהודה would adorn it with students; רב חסדא would adorn it with cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list of ten and explains עיטור, showing how two אמוראים carried it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עיטור means giving the כוס של ברכה honor by surrounding it with something. רב יהודה surrounded himself with students while making the ברכה. רב חסדא placed other cups of wine around the כוס של ברכה.

phrases.english: Adorning.
phrases.notes: Quoting the item from the list in step 25.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would adorn it with students,
Rav Chisda would adorn it with cups.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיטּוּר. רַב יְהוּדָה מְעַטְּרֵהוּ בְּתַלְמִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of ten in step 25 to explain עיטור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיטור can be done by surrounding the cup with students or with other cups.

steps.title: רבי חנן adds: with undiluted wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן adds a short point: 'and with חי,' meaning the wine involved should be undiluted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said: And with undiluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנן adds a brief condition to what was just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reading takes this as adding to רב חסדא's practice: the cups surrounding the כוס של ברכה should also hold undiluted wine. Other commentators connect it to the חי requirement for the cup itself, which רב ששת then clarifies in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanan said: And with undiluted wine.
phrases.notes: A very short addition; the next step builds on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן: וּבְחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition about undiluted wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine involved should be undiluted.

steps.title: רב ששת: at the blessing of the land
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds: 'and in ברכת הארץ,' which connects the wine requirement to the second ברכה of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: And in the blessing of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a timing detail to the previous comment about undiluted wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רש״י, the wine stays undiluted (חי) until ברכת הארץ, and water is added at that point. The comment links the cup's condition to a specific point in ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of the land, the second ברכה of ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: This line is very short and is explained in different ways. Do not assume it creates a new eleventh requirement. It only adds a detail to the comment about חי.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: And in the blessing of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וּבְבִרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds when the חי condition applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חי requirement is tied to ברכת הארץ (according to רש״י, undiluted until then, and water is added there).

steps.title: How the leader wrapped himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains עיטוף: רב פפא wrapped himself and sat, and רב אסי spread a cloth over his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wrapping: רב פפא would wrap himself and sit. רב אסי would spread a cloth on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item from the list, עיטוף, using the practice of two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עיטוף means the person leading the ברכה covers himself out of respect. רב פפא wrapped himself (in his garment, or טלית) and sat while saying it. רב אסי spread a cloth over his head. Both are ways of showing honor for the ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: עיטור honors the cup (with students or other cups), and עיטוף honors the person blessing (by covering himself or his head).

phrases.english: Wrapping.
phrases.notes: Quoting the next item from the list in step 25.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa would wrap himself and sit.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַסִּי פָּרֵיס סוּדָרָא עַל רֵישֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Asi would spread a cloth on his head.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיטּוּף. רַב פָּפָּא מִעַטַּף וְיָתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next term in the list of ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיטוף is done by wrapping oneself or covering the head with a cloth.

steps.title: A verse as the source for lifting the cup with both hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the practice 'he takes it in his two hands.' רבי חיננא בר פפא brings the פסוק 'Lift your hands in holiness and bless ה׳' as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He takes it in his two hands.' רבי חיננא בר פפא said: What is the verse for this? 'Lift your hands in holiness and bless ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next practice on the list for the כוס של ברכה: lifting the cup with both hands. It gives a פסוק that hints at this practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of lifting 'your hands' (plural) while blessing ה׳. So the person saying ברכת המזון lifts the cup with both hands. The question 'מאי קראה' is not a challenge. It is a request for a scriptural source, and רבי חיננא answers it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes it (the cup) with both of his hands
What is the verse? (a request for a source in תנ״ך)
Lift your hands in holiness (תהלים קל״ד:ב)

phrases.english: He takes it in his two hands.
phrases.notes: Quoting the next item in the list of practices for the כוס של ברכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥinnana bar Pappa said:
What is the verse?
phrases.notes: He's just asking which פסוק this comes from, not raising a challenge.

phrases.english: "Lift your hands in holiness
and bless the Lord."
phrases.notes: תהלים קל״ד:ב. The plural 'hands' points to using both hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of כוס של ברכה practices after עיטור and עיטוף, moving on to how the cup is held.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cup of blessing is lifted with both hands, based on 'שאו ידיכם קדש וברכו את ה׳'.

steps.title: May the left hand help the right in holding the cup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the practice 'and he places it in the right hand.' רבי יוחנן reports that the early sages asked whether the left hand may assist the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he places it in the right hand.' רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The early sages asked: May the left hand help the right?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next practice: after lifting the cup with both hands, the person puts it into his right hand. A question is then raised about whether the left hand may support the right hand while he holds it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the cup is in the right hand, it is unclear whether the left hand must be removed completely. The other option is that it may still give support. The ראשונים asked this question, and as the next step shows, they never resolved it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he places it into the right hand
The early sages (earlier generations of חכמים)
May the left hand assist the right?

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רִאשׁוֹנִים' means earlier sages of the תלמוד era. It does not mean the medieval commentators (רש״י, תוספות, etc.) whom we usually call ראשונים.

phrases.english: And he places it in the right hand.
phrases.notes: Quoting the next item in the list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The early sages asked:
What is the law, may the left hand assist the right?

steps.triggerLanguage: רִאשׁוֹנִים שָׁאֲלוּ: שְׂמֹאל מַהוּ שֶׁתְּסַיֵּיעַ לַיָּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from holding the cup with both hands. Now the cup goes to the right hand, which raises the question of what the left hand may do.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the left hand may help support the cup once it is placed in the right hand.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a ruling based on the unresolved question
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to give a practical ruling. Since the early sages raised this question and never resolved it, a conclusion will follow, and it appears on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Since the early sages had this question and it was not resolved for them,
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens his response to the unresolved question. This line is a setup: it gives his reason, and the actual ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not try to solve the question himself. Instead, he treats the fact that it was never settled as the basis for how we should act in practice. The words 'הואיל' (since) signal that a practical conclusion is about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: It was a question for them (an unresolved dilemma)
And it was not resolved for them

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Since the early sages raised this dilemma
and it was not resolved for them,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with רב אשי's practical conclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הוֹאִיל וְרִאשׁוֹנִים אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ וְלֹא אִיפְּשִׁט לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the unresolved question of the ראשונים by starting a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the question about the left hand helping was never resolved, רב אשי bases a practical ruling on that doubt. The ruling itself appears on the next amud.
